summary: The lecture covers communication systems in India, distinguishing personal (post, telegraph, telephone, internet) and mass communication (newspaper, radio, TV, satellite). It details the evolution of Indian postal, telegraph, telephone, internet, radio, television, and satellite systems with key dates, organizations, and technical terms relevant for competitive exams.
points: Indian Postal System is world's largest with ~1.5 lakh post offices covering entire country.
First Post Office in India established in 1764 at Calcutta (Kolkata).
Postal network formally established in 1837; first Indian postal stamp issued in 1852 at Karachi.
PIN code introduced in 1972; Speed Post (Quick Mail Service) started in 1975.
First telegraph service in India: 1854, Mumbai to Pune.
First telephone exchange: 1883, Calcutta by Oriental Telephone Company.
First internet service in India: 1995 provided by BSNL/VSNL.
All India Radio formed 1936, renamed Akashvani in 1957.
First television operational 1959; Doordarshan national programme (Common National Programme) from 1976.
INSAT (Indian National Satellite System) for telecom established 1983; IRS (Indian Remote Sensing Satellite System) for remote sensing established 1988.
ISRO established 1969; National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) located in Hyderabad.
STD = Subscriber Trunk Dialling (domestic); ISD = International Subscriber Dialling (international).
